newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker, NY fails to inspire.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker, NY fails to inspire.

text.p: White sugar futures retained their earlier slight weakness on Friday afternoon, trapped in the recent stifling ranges and waiting for the New York funds to make the first move.
London's spot May contract burst higher during Thursday's session, bolted into action when a combination of local shortcovering and fund buying pushed May raws briefly above the 11.00 cents/lb mark.
But on Friday both markets lapsed back into place, with London trading a technically inside day in a tight range of just 90 cents basis May.
"It's a litle bit disappointing. The trouble is it's rangebound, we had a little bit of action yesterday which probably tied everybody up," one trader said.
Market sources said the raws market would need to break the range first, as and when the fund players decided to make their move.
On the upside, May would have to challenge 11.00 cents for a second time, otherwise the market could easily drift lower, they said.
In London, one large against actuals trade between a commission and trade house, notched up during morning trading, provided around half of the entire volume.
At 1655 GMT May was down 30 cents at $306.40 and August down 30 cents at $305.00. The AA accounted for 183 of the 363 lots posted on the board.
Trading in Paris was similarly subdued and price movements were equally tight.
May was down 50 cents at $306.00 and August down 30 cents at $305.20. Matif volume reached a scant 130 lots.
